cards.explanation: The answer is that his only daughter is dying. Jairus, a synagogue leader, falls at Jesus' feet and begs, and the text gives the reason: “…his only daughter, who was about twelve, was dying.” (Luke 8:42) A man in his position drops to the ground in front of everybody. I think that tells you how much he needed Jesus to come.

The answer is twelve. Luke says the girl “…was about twelve…” so the text gives us a rough age, not an exact one. Jairus' only daughter is right on the edge of growing up. I think that makes his begging hit even harder.

The answer is physicians. Luke says she “…had spent all her money on physicians…” (Luke 8:43) That's every last coin, handed over to doctors in hope of getting better. I think she was running out of places to turn.

The answer is False. The text says she “…had spent all her money on physicians, but no one was able to heal her.” (Luke 8:43) Twelve years, all her money, and still no healing. So whatever happens next, it won't come from the doctors.

The answer is the fringe of His cloak. The woman “…came up behind Jesus and touched the fringe of His cloak…” (Luke 8:44) The very next thing Luke says is “…immediately her bleeding stopped.” Big moment, friends.

The answer is immediately, friends! The text says she touched the fringe and “…immediately her bleeding stopped.” (Luke 8:44) No waiting around and no slow improvement. After twelve years, it stopped on the spot.
The answer is that they all deny it. When Jesus asks “Who touched Me?” the text says, “…they all denied it.” (Luke 8:45) Everybody in that crowd says it wasn't them. Nobody has stepped forward yet.

The answer is that power has gone out from Him. Jesus says, “Someone touched Me, for I know that power has gone out from Me.” (Luke 8:46) That's the reason He gives for knowing. The crowds are pressing around Him, and still He says someone touched Him.

The answer is True. Luke says that “In the presence of all the people, she explained why she had touched Him and how she had immediately been healed.” (Luke 8:47) She came trembling, and she still told it with all those people there. I think that took a lot of courage.
The answer is her faith, friends. Jesus says, “Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace.” (Luke 8:48) He names it plainly. Twelve years of no answers, and He sends her off with this.
The answer is that his daughter is dead. The messenger tells Jairus, “Your daughter is dead…” (Luke 8:49) This is a heavy moment. I think this one hurts, so let's give it room.

The answer is False. The messenger tells Jairus, “Your daughter is dead…” and then, “Do not bother the Teacher anymore.” (Luke 8:49) There's no hurry in it, only a stop sign. But Jesus overhears, and He has something different to say.

The answer is that He tells Jairus not to be afraid and just believe. Jesus overhears and says, “Do not be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed.” (Luke 8:50) He says it right after the news that the girl is dead. Jairus doesn't have to carry that alone.

The answer is False. Luke says that when Jesus entered the house, “…He did not allow anyone to go in with Him except Peter, John, James, and the child’s father and mother.” (Luke 8:51) It's a very short list. Think of a packed room that suddenly gets quiet.
The answer is mother. Jesus allows only Peter, John, James, “…and the child’s father and mother.” (Luke 8:51) So both of her parents are in the room. Peter, John and James are three of His disciples.

The answer is that she is not dead but asleep. While everyone is weeping and mourning, Jesus says, “Stop weeping; she is not dead but asleep.” (Luke 8:52) It's a surprising thing to say in that room. Keep going, friends, because the next verses show what He means.
The answer is laugh. Luke says, “And they laughed at Him, knowing that she was dead.” (Luke 8:53) Their laughing comes right after Jesus says she is asleep. Jesus keeps going anyway.

The answer is get up. Jesus takes her by the hand and calls out, “Child, get up!” (Luke 8:54) Simple words, spoken while holding her hand. Next Luke says, “Her spirit returned, and at once she got up.” (Luke 8:55)
The answer is True. Luke says, “Her spirit returned, and at once she got up.” (Luke 8:55) No delay at all. Jesus called, and she got up.

The answer is to give her something to eat. Luke says Jesus “…directed that she be given something to eat.” (Luke 8:55) She has just gotten up, and that's the instruction Jesus gives about her. I think that's about as caring as it gets.

The answer is False. Luke says that her parents were astounded, “…but Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.” (Luke 8:56) The instruction is to keep quiet. The text doesn't give a reason, so we won't guess one.
